appraisal_events.evidence: Certes, une femme élégante, Albertine peu à peu en devenait une. Car si chaque chose que je lui faisais faire ainsi était en son genre la plus jolie, avec tous les raffinements qu'y eussent apportés Mme de Guermantes ou Mme Swann...
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator describes Albertine steadily becoming a genuinely elegant woman under his cultivation, her acquired taste matching the refinement one would expect from figures as eminent as Mme de Guermantes or Mme Swann.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Je suis épouvantée en pensant que sans vous je serais restée stupide... Vous m'avez ouvert un monde d'idées que je ne soupçonnais pas, et le peu que je suis devenue, je ne le dois qu'à vous. » On sait qu'elle avait parlé semblablement de mon influence sur Andrée.
appraisal_events.explanation: Albertine credits the narrator effusively for her intellectual awakening, but the narrator flags her as mistaken and notes she made the identical claim about her debt to him regarding Andrée, undercutting the sincerity and singularity of the praise.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine is locally elevated as her taste and manner develop into genuine elegance comparable to that of the era's most refined women.

Her declaration of intellectual debt to the narrator is deflated by the revelation that she used the same words about her influence on Andrée, making the sentiment look formulaic rather than singular.

ambiguities: Albertine's praise of the narrator in E2 is explicitly ironized ('en se trompant') and echoed elsewhere with Andrée, so whether it reflects any real elevation of the narrator himself, or purely exposes Albertine's interchangeable sincerity, is left uncertain by the text.
